story.iWant: a clear separation between internal development documentation and user-facing documentation
story.soThat: I can protect confidential information, maintain documentation quality, and provide users with a clean experience

task.title: Audit current documentation structure
task.subtask: List all files in docs/ directory
Categorize each file as INTERNAL or USER-FACING
Document classification decisions with rationale

task.title: Create new directory structure
task.subtask: Create docs/internal/ directory
Create subdirectories: planning/, sprint-artifacts/, reports/, design/
Create user-facing subdirectories: validation/, guides/, examples/

task.title: Move internal documents
task.subtask: Move PRD and architecture docs to docs/internal/planning/
Move epics and stories to docs/internal/planning/epics/
Move sprint artifacts to docs/internal/sprint-artifacts/
Use git mv to preserve history

task.title: Update cross-references
task.subtask: Update all internal document links
Update all user-facing document links
Run link checker to verify no broken links

task.title: Update documentation generation configs
task.subtask: Update MkDocs/pdoc configuration
Update .gitignore if needed
Update CI/CD documentation pipelines
Update README entry point links

task.title: Verify no confidential content exposed
task.subtask: Review all user-facing docs for internal references
Remove or redact any business strategy/timeline content
Confirm user docs are standalone and useful

task.title: Testing
task.subtask: Build documentation locally and verify structure
Verify internal docs are properly protected
Run documentation generation and verify output

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Internal documents are in a dedicated docs/internal/ directory
User-facing documents are in the main docs/ directory with clear structure
Documentation generation configs (YAML files) are updated to reflect the new structure
No internal/confidential content is exposed in user-facing docs
All internal cross-references are updated and functional
All user-facing cross-references are updated and functional
INTERNAL classification applied to: PRD, architecture, epics, sprint-artifacts, BMM files
USER-FACING classification applied to: guides, API reference, tutorials, examples, contributing
MkDocs/pdoc config, .gitignore, CI/CD pipelines, README links updated

doc.title: Architecture Document
doc.snippet: Defines dual-location architecture: rustybt/validation/ (library) + tests/validation/ (tests). Documentation lives in docs/ with validation/ subdirectory for validation framework docs.

doc.title: Product Requirements Document
doc.snippet: FR65 requires user-facing documentation of DESIGN differences. NFR16 requires clear and actionable test reports.

doc.title: Epic 8 Definition
doc.snippet: Defines proposed structure: docs/internal/ for protected content, docs/validation/ for user-facing validation docs.

file.reason: MkDocs and Sphinx documentation dependencies configuration

constraints.constraint: Dual-location architecture: validation framework library in rustybt/validation/, tests in tests/validation/
Validation session storage at validation-sessions/ should remain gitignored
Documentation must be clear and actionable (NFR16)
Internal docs include: PRD, architecture, epics, sprint-artifacts, BMM files, project scan reports
User-facing docs include: getting started guides, API reference, tutorials, examples, contributing guidelines

tests.standards: Use link-checking tools to validate all internal and external links after reorganization. Documentation builds must succeed with new structure. No false positives or false negatives in content classification.

ideas.idea: Test that docs/internal/ exists and contains expected internal documents
Verify MkDocs/pdoc builds successfully with new config
Audit user-facing docs for any internal references
Run link checker to verify all cross-references are functional
Verify CI/CD documentation pipeline works with new structure
